records.name: Albina
records.facts_used: Albina: Lithuanian Albina continues the feminine form of Roman Albinus. Albinus is connected with Latin albus, white. The family’s lexical origin does not describe every bearer’s appearance; it explains the historical name formation. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Albina (Albė) on 16 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Salys PDF 319/printed 304 December 16 Albina(Albė); DMNES corroborates albus. Masculine 763 Albinus is not a first Lithuanian female date.

records.name: Adelheid
records.facts_used: Adelheid: The Estonian name is linked to the Adelheid family and its short forms. The Germanic full name combines adal, noble, and heit, kind or nature. Short forms need not retain both elements; French Adèle is a related name in the adal family. The first page of Leole’s December 2005 issue uses the exact spelling Adelheid. The local name column shows that this form was discussed in Estonian print. This dated evidence is neither a first birth record nor the year the name was invented.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact local Leole 2005 p 1 forms; noble adal plus full Adelheid heit explained without treating every short form as a two-stem compound. German Adelheid and French Adèle are cognate routes, not a false claim that German Adelheid derives from French Adèle.
